title: Projectile motion; Forces and free-body diagrams; Newton's first law and equilibrium; Newton's second law; Drag and terminal velocity; Moments and static equilibrium; Systems and centre of mass
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for OCR A-level (A) Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: D01-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; K04-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; D01-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; K04-1#t4 term and clue written for the game. Questions: D01-1#N.6a, D02-1#N.2, D03-1#N.2, D07-1#N.2, D08-1#N.2, D11-1#N.3, D01-1#N.9, D02-1#N.4, D03-1#N.7a, D07-1#N.5, D08-1#N.5a, D11-1#N.14.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Mass
items.clue: Amount of matter in an object, in kg; the same everywhere.

items.label: Range
items.clue: Horizontal distance a projectile covers between launch and landing.

items.label: Tension
items.clue: Pull of a string, rope or cable, acting along it and away from the object.

items.label: Horizontal component
items.clue: Part of the launch velocity that never changes, as no force acts that way.

questions.stem: A space probe weighs 4905 N on Earth, where g = 9.81 N kg⁻¹. It lands on Mars, where g = 3.7 N kg⁻¹. What is the probe's mass on Mars?

options.text: 190 kg
500 kg

questions.explanation: m = W/g on Earth = 500 kg. Mass does not depend on location, so it is still 500 kg on Mars (where it weighs 500 × 3.7 = 1850 N).

questions.stem: A space probe is so far from any star or planet that the forces exerted on it are negligible. Its engines fire briefly and then shut off. Which statement describes the probe's motion after the engines have shut off?

options.text: It slows down and stops, as all moving objects do in time.
It slows down as the force from the engine firing is used up.
It moves in a straight line at a constant speed.
It stops almost at once, as no force now pushes it forward.

questions.stem: A crate slides to the left across a level floor with negligible friction. At one instant, two students push on it horizontally: one pushes to the left with a force of 20 N, and the other pushes to the right with a force of 30 N. Which statement about the crate at this instant is correct?

options.text: Its speed is increasing, as there is a net force exerted on it.
Its acceleration is to the left, the direction it is moving.
Its speed is decreasing, as its acceleration is to the right.
Its speed is constant, as the net force exerted on it is constant.

questions.stem: A cylindrical rod is made of a 0.50 m aluminium section joined end to end to a 0.50 m steel section of the same diameter. Each section is uniform, and the steel section has the greater mass. How does the location of the rod's centre of mass compare with the rod's midpoint?

options.text: It is at the midpoint, since the rod's shape is symmetric about that point.
It is on the aluminium side of the midpoint, nearer the lighter section.
It is at the centre of the steel section, the more massive part.
It lies between the midpoint and the centre of the steel section.

questions.stem: A mechanic pulls with a 20 N force on the end of a tool handle, 0.25 m from the centre of a nut. The force is in the plane of the handle's turn, but at 30° to the handle instead of at 90°. What is the turning effect of the force about the centre of the nut?

options.text: 5.0 N m
4.3 N m
80 N m
2.5 N m

questions.explanation: Perpendicular distance = 0.25 × sin 30° = 0.125 m, so the turning effect = 20 × 0.125 = 2.5 N m.

questions.stem: A small steel ball is released from rest in air and falls until it reaches terminal velocity. How does its acceleration change during this time?

options.text: It is constant but less than g, because drag is constant.
It stays equal to g, since drag only lowers the ball's speed.
It increases, since the ball moves faster and faster as it falls.
It decreases from g towards zero as the drag increases.

questions.explanation: At release the ball is at rest, so there is no drag and its acceleration is g. As it speeds up the drag grows, so the acceleration decreases, reaching zero at terminal velocity.

questions.stem: A ball has been thrown straight up and is still rising. Air resistance is not negligible; the upthrust of the air is negligible. Which list gives all the forces acting on the ball, and no others?

options.text: Weight downwards and an upward force from the throw
Weight downwards and drag upwards
Weight and drag, both downwards
Weight only

questions.explanation: Earth pulls down; drag opposes the velocity, which is upwards, so drag also points down. Both slow the ball.

questions.stem: A puck slides east at constant velocity across level ice with negligible friction. Starting at time t, a constant force directed north is exerted on the puck, and no other horizontal force acts. Which statement describes the puck's motion after time t?

options.text: It turns and moves due north, in the direction of the force on it.
Its eastward velocity decreases while its northward velocity increases.
It moves at a constant velocity in a direction between east and north.
Its eastward velocity stays the same while its northward velocity increases.

questions.stem: Block X (2.0 kg) and block Y (4.0 kg) rest on a frictionless horizontal surface, joined by a light string. A horizontal force of 24 N pulls X away from Y, and both accelerate together. What is the tension in the string?
questions.explanation: System: a = 24 ÷ 6.0 = 4.0 m s⁻². Y alone: the only horizontal force is the tension, T = 4.0 × 4.0 = 16 N.

questions.stem: A rectangular wooden sign hangs from a single hook through a hole at the middle of its top edge. A heavy metal letter is fixed near the sign's left end. How does the sign hang at rest?

options.text: Level, because the hook is at the middle of the top edge.
Tilted, left end lower, with its centre of gravity directly below the hook.
Tilted, left end lower, until the metal letter is directly below the hook.
Tilted, right end lower, to balance the heavy letter.

questions.explanation: At rest the weight has no moment about the hook, so its line of action passes through the hook. The sign turns until its centre of gravity, shifted left by the letter, is vertically below the hook.

questions.stem: A uniform beam of length 5.0 m and weight 400 N rests horizontally on two supports, one at each end, P and Q. A person of weight 600 N stands on the beam 1.0 m from Q. What is the upward force from support P?
questions.explanation: Taking moments about Q: F_P × 5.0 = 400 × 2.5 + 600 × 1.0 = 1600 N m, so F_P = 320 N.

questions.stem: Two paper cones have the same size and shape. A second cone is pushed inside one of them, doubling its mass without changing its outside shape. Both are dropped from a high balcony. Which statement about their terminal velocities is correct?

options.text: Both reach the same terminal velocity, as all objects in free fall have the same acceleration.
The double cone reaches a higher terminal velocity, as drag must grow to equal a weight twice as large.
The double cone reaches a lower terminal velocity, as its greater weight gives it more drag at every speed.
The double cone reaches its terminal velocity sooner, as its greater weight gives it a greater acceleration from the start.
